text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak will have talks in Paris with President Jacques Chirac after attending the annual meeting of the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said that for the first time in history industry's contribution to the economy has overtaken that of agriculture, at 22 percent of GDP against 21 percent for agriculture.
- Justice Minister Farouk Seiful-Nasr said there would be legislative changes to speed up the legal system.
- From next year onwards workers will need licences to work in the building trade and in contracting.
- Prime Minister Ganzouri has approved three new industrial zones -- one at Gamasa on the Delta coast and two in Beni Suef province south of Cairo.
- President Chirac will meet Mubarak next Monday.
- A visiting British official said that the Standard and Poor's rating for Egypt had created a postive atmosphere in London markets and drawn the attention of investors to Egypt.
- Production of bottled gas has been increased by 104,000 cylinders a day to meet winter demand

- The draft investment law goes to the cabinet today. The cabinet will also discuss a report on the obstacles to carrying out cabinet decisions taken last year on streamlining bureaucracy and making services easier to obtain.

- Electricity Minister Maher Abaza said that Egypt will export electricity from next year and that all facilities will be given to encourage the private sector to set up electricity projects. The first BOT power station will be offered to tender in September, he added.
